parallel.requirements: Recognized the required pure Rust 2021 migration, std-only constraint, root test11.rs, modular Cargo project, black-box inference from the executable, atoi-style parsing, and byte-identical output with trailing spaces.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation, integration, verification, and final delivery ownership while spawning two helpers for pattern probing and implementation strategy.
parallel.implementation: The parent sampled many n values and edge cases, implemented gear polygon generation, a pure-std ear clipper, and C atoi-like parsing, then fixed module paths for Cargo and standalone rustc.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent wrote Cargo.toml, src modules, and test11.rs in /output, built target/release/test11 and test11_bin, and delivered those files in the final artifact.
parallel.verification: It ran cargo test, cargo build --release, rustc test11.rs, and a Perl byte-for-byte comparison against the C++ executable over sampled normal and edge inputs.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No task-relevant unfinished work remained at closure; the only interrupted child was redundant probing after the parent had a verified candidate.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Rust 2021, std-only, root test11.rs, Cargo project, black-box inference, atoi-compatible CLI, and exact output requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned the whole pipeline from sampling and inference through implementation, build, verification, and final delivery.
serial.implementation: The serial run sampled the reference binary, probed atoi overflow behavior with a tiny C program, implemented modules for atoi, geometry, triangulation, and the root binary.
serial.integration_and_delivery: It created Cargo.toml, src/atoi.rs, src/geometry.rs, src/triangulation.rs, src/lib.rs, and test11.rs, then produced Cargo and rustc executables.
serial.verification: It built with Cargo and rustc, compared the Cargo binary against the C++ executable over default, 0..20, malformed, signed, and negative arguments, and spot-checked the rustc binary output.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No visible task-relevant unfinished work remained at closure; the current official evaluator passed all testcases.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Current completed cell/status.json evaluations show both attempts passed all 40 official testcases. The parallel run differed mainly by using advisory and probing child agents, while the serial run kept the same inference, implementation, integration, and verification work local. Because both delivered verified byte-identical Rust implementations and both official evaluations passed, there is no discordant outcome and no parallel-side coordination failure needed to explain a score difference.
